title: Princely states of India
summary: When the British Crown took over from the East India Company in 1858, it did not rule all of India directly. About two-fifths of the subcontinent stayed under Indian princes: maharajas, nawabs, the Nizam of Hyderabad and hundreds of minor chiefs. Many of their states had signed 'subsidiary alliances' with the Company, giving up control of foreign affairs and accepting British troops in return for protection. After 1858 the Crown inherited these treaties and claimed 'paramountcy': the rulers ran their own internal affairs, but Britain controlled their defence and foreign relations, kept a Resident or Political Agent at their courts, and could depose a ruler for misrule. In 1947 there were 565 recognised states, from Hyderabad and Kashmir, each larger than many European countries, to estates of a few villages. When British rule ended, paramountcy lapsed and each ruler was asked to join India or Pakistan. Most signed Instruments of Accession by 15 August 1947. Junagadh's Nawab chose Pakistan, but India took over in November 1947; Kashmir's Maharaja acceded to India in October 1947 during a tribal invasion; Kalat joined Pakistan in March 1948; and Hyderabad was taken over by the Indian Army in September 1948. These outlines are traced from the Imperial Gazetteer of India maps of 1909 and from OpenHistoricalMap. The largest states are drawn singly; the hundreds of small ones are grouped by agency. Boundaries are approximate, and they show the states as they were around 1909.

regions.name: Hyderabad
regions.note: The Nizam's state in the Deccan, one of the two largest princely states with Jammu and Kashmir. The Nizam did not accede in 1947; the Indian Army took control between 13 and 18 September 1948 (Operation Polo). Outline from OpenHistoricalMap, matching the 1909 Imperial Gazetteer map; Berar is shown separately. Drawn area c. 213,900 km².

regions.name: Berar (Hyderabad Assigned Districts)
regions.note: Assigned by the Nizam to East India Company administration under an 1853 treaty, so it was Hyderabad's territory but British-run. Leased permanently to the British on 5 November 1902 and joined to the Central Provinces from 1 October 1903. Drawn area c. 43,600 km².

regions.name: Mysore (under British commission)
regions.capital: Mysore (Bangalore was the seat of the British commission 1831–1881)
regions.note: The British took over direct administration of Mysore in 1831. The state kept its identity and was handed back (the 'rendition') in 1881 to Chamarajendra Wadiyar X. Drawn area c. 79,600 km².

regions.name: Mysore
regions.note: Ruled again by the Wodeyar dynasty after the 1881 rendition; one of the largest states in the south. Joined the Indian Union on 9 August 1947. Drawn area c. 79,600 km².

regions.name: Jammu and Kashmir
regions.note: Ruled by the Dogra maharajas, including Ladakh and the Gilgit region (the outline follows OpenHistoricalMap and includes claimed frontier areas). Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession to India dated 26 October 1947; Mountbatten accepted it on 27 October. Drawn area c. 186,200 km².

regions.name: Cochin
regions.note: Small kingdom north of Travancore, around Ernakulam and Trichur. It acceded to India in 1947 and merged with Travancore on 1 July 1949. Its boundary with Travancore is approximate (traced from the 1909 Madras map). Drawn area c. 3,100 km².

regions.name: Travancore
regions.note: Southern kingdom on the Malabar coast. Its ruler agreed to accede to India on 12 August 1947; it merged with Cochin on 1 July 1949. Outline from OpenHistoricalMap, with the Cochin part cut off along the 1909 map's boundary (approximate). Drawn area c. 20,000 km².

regions.name: Cutch
regions.note: Peninsula state ruled by the Rao; the outline includes the Great Rann. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 42,200 km².

regions.name: Kolhapur
regions.note: Maratha state of the Bhonsle line of Shivaji, the chief state of the Kolhapur and Southern Maratha Country agency. Outline from OpenHistoricalMap. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 7,700 km².

regions.name: Sikkim
regions.note: Himalayan kingdom, a British protectorate from the 1861 Treaty of Tumlong. It did not join India in 1947; it became an Indian protectorate in 1950 and an Indian state in 1975. Drawn area c. 7,100 km².

regions.name: Manipur
regions.note: Hill kingdom on the Burma frontier. Acceded to India on 11 August 1947. Drawn area c. 22,400 km².

regions.name: Hill Tippera (Tripura)
regions.note: Kingdom east of Bengal, called Hill Tippera in British records. Acceded to India on 13 August 1947. Drawn area c. 10,500 km².

regions.name: Bahawalpur
regions.note: Muslim-ruled state on the Sutlej, south-west of the Punjab. The Nawab signed accession to Pakistan on 5 October 1947, accepted on 9 October; the first state to accede to Pakistan. Drawn area c. 45,000 km².

regions.name: Khairpur
regions.note: State of the Talpur Mirs in Sind. Acceded to Pakistan on 3 October 1947. Drawn area c. 16,200 km².

regions.name: Kalat (with Kharan, Las Bela and Makran)
regions.note: The Khan of Kalat headed a confederacy of Baloch chiefs; Kharan, Las Bela and Makran are included in this outline (Kharan was separated from Kalat as its own state in the 1930s). Kharan, Las Bela and Makran acceded to Pakistan first; Kalat acceded on 27 March 1948. Kalat, Kharan and Las Bela outlines are from OpenHistoricalMap; Makran is traced from the 1909 map. Drawn area c. 191,500 km².

regions.name: Chitral
regions.note: Mountain state of the Mehtar, allied with the British from 1885 (agreement of 1891). The Mehtar signed the Instrument of Accession to Pakistan on 6 November 1947. The outline is hand-drawn from the 1909 North-West Frontier Province map and is larger than the 14,860 km² given for 1951. Drawn area c. 19,000 km².

regions.name: Bikaner
regions.note: Rathore state in the Thar Desert, in the Rajputana Agency. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 59,100 km².

regions.name: Jaisalmer
regions.note: Bhati Rajput desert state in the Rajputana Agency. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 40,000 km².

regions.name: Jodhpur (Marwar)
regions.note: The largest state in Rajputana, ruled by Rathores. Acceded to India in August 1947. Drawn area c. 92,400 km².

regions.name: Jaipur
regions.note: Kachhwaha state, including the Shekhawati chiefships. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 34,400 km².

regions.name: Udaipur (Mewar)
regions.note: Senior Rajput house (Sisodias) in the Aravalli hills. The small state of Shahpura sits inside this outline. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 32,600 km².

regions.name: Kotah (with Jhalawar)
regions.note: Kotah and Jhalawar (carved out of Kotah) formed the Kotah and Jhalawar Agency; they are drawn together because their boundary cannot be read reliably on the 1909 map. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 17,500 km².

regions.name: Gwalior
regions.note: Maratha state of the Scindias. This outline is the main northern block (Gwalior, Bhind, Sheopur, Narwar, Isagarh); Gwalior's Malwa districts (Ujjain, Mandsaur, Shajapur and others) are interleaved with other states and are inside the Central India group. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 33,600 km².

regions.name: Indore
regions.note: Maratha state of the Holkars. Outline is the main Indore–Nimar block; detached parts (such as Rampura-Bhanpura) are inside the Central India group. Its edges are approximate. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 12,500 km².

regions.name: Bhopal
regions.note: Muslim-ruled state, for much of the 19th century governed by begums. Its edges are approximate. Shown until 1947 with the other Central India states. Drawn area c. 14,800 km².

regions.name: Rewa
regions.note: The largest state in Baghelkhand. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 34,400 km².

regions.name: Baroda (Amreli)
regions.note: A detached division of Baroda, the Gaekwad's Maratha state, whose territory lay in separate blocks across Gujarat and Kathiawar. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 2,800 km².

regions.name: Baroda (Okhamandal)
regions.note: A detached division of Baroda, the Gaekwad's Maratha state, whose territory lay in separate blocks across Gujarat and Kathiawar. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 600 km².

regions.name: Baroda (Kodinar)
regions.note: A detached division of Baroda, the Gaekwad's Maratha state, whose territory lay in separate blocks across Gujarat and Kathiawar. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 500 km².

regions.name: Baroda (Amreli)
regions.note: A detached division of Baroda, the Gaekwad's Maratha state, whose territory lay in separate blocks across Gujarat and Kathiawar. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 300 km².

regions.name: Baroda (Kadi division)
regions.note: A detached division of Baroda, the Gaekwad's Maratha state, whose territory lay in separate blocks across Gujarat and Kathiawar. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 8,600 km².

regions.name: Baroda (Baroda division)
regions.note: A detached division of Baroda, the Gaekwad's Maratha state, whose territory lay in separate blocks across Gujarat and Kathiawar. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 4,100 km².

regions.name: Baroda (Navsari division)
regions.note: A detached division of Baroda, the Gaekwad's Maratha state, whose territory lay in separate blocks across Gujarat and Kathiawar. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 3,100 km².

regions.name: Junagadh
regions.note: Muslim-ruled state on the Kathiawar peninsula. The Nawab acceded to Pakistan, fled on 26 October 1947, and on 7 November 1947 the state's council invited India to take over; a February 1948 plebiscite favoured India. Edges approximate. Drawn area c. 7,400 km².

regions.name: Bastar
regions.note: The largest of the Chhattisgarh feudatory states, a forested plateau. Merged into the Central Provinces on 1 January 1948 after acceding in 1947. Drawn area c. 32,200 km².

regions.name: Surguja
regions.note: Hill state of the Chota Nagpur plateau, among the Central Provinces feudatories in 1909. Merged on 1 January 1948. Drawn area c. 13,300 km².

regions.name: Mayurbhanj
regions.note: The largest of the Orissa feudatory states. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 9,200 km².

regions.name: Patiala
regions.note: The leading Sikh (Phulkian) state. The outline is its main block; the small states of Nabha and Malerkotla, which lie in pockets within it, are not separated. Patiala's Narnaul district lies far to the south (not shown separately). Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 15,000 km².

regions.name: Tehri Garhwal
regions.note: Hill state in the Himalaya north of Dehra Dun, under the United Provinces. Traced from the small-scale 1909 empire map only, so its outline is coarse. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 9,500 km².

regions.name: Pudukkottai
regions.note: The only princely state in the Tamil country, under the Madras government. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 3,200 km².

regions.name: Rajputana Agency (other states): Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur, Karauli, Bundi, Tonk
regions.note: Smaller states of the Rajputana Agency, grouped because their boundaries cannot be drawn singly at the scale of the 1909 map. All acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 32,800 km².

regions.name: Rajputana Agency (other states): Dungarpur, Banswara, Partabgarh
regions.note: Smaller states of the Rajputana Agency, grouped because their boundaries cannot be drawn singly at the scale of the 1909 map. All acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 14,000 km².

regions.name: Rajputana Agency (other states): Sirohi
regions.note: Smaller states of the Rajputana Agency, grouped because their boundaries cannot be drawn singly at the scale of the 1909 map. All acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 6,900 km².

regions.name: Rajputana Agency (other states): Kishangarh
regions.note: Smaller states of the Rajputana Agency, grouped because their boundaries cannot be drawn singly at the scale of the 1909 map. All acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 4,600 km².

regions.name: Rajputana Agency (other states): detached tracts near Pirawa and Gangdhar
regions.note: Smaller states of the Rajputana Agency, grouped because their boundaries cannot be drawn singly at the scale of the 1909 map. All acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 3,000 km².

regions.name: Rajputana Agency (other states): Tonk (Sironj)
regions.note: Smaller states of the Rajputana Agency, grouped because their boundaries cannot be drawn singly at the scale of the 1909 map. All acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 2,700 km².

regions.name: Rajputana Agency (other states): Tonk (Chhabra)
regions.note: Smaller states of the Rajputana Agency, grouped because their boundaries cannot be drawn singly at the scale of the 1909 map. All acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 1,200 km².

regions.name: Central India Agency (other states): Dewas, Dhar, Ratlam, Jaora, Rajgarh, Sitamau, Jhabua, Alirajpur, Barwani, Sailana, Kurwai, Gwalior (Ujjain district), Gwalior (Mandsaur district)
regions.note: Smaller states of the Central India Agency (Malwa, Bhopawar, Bundelkhand and Baghelkhand agencies), with the detached Malwa districts of Gwalior and Indore. The many small states and interlocking enclaves cannot be drawn singly from the 1909 map. All acceded in 1947–48. Drawn area c. 71,600 km².

regions.name: Central India Agency (other states): Orchha, Panna, Chhatarpur, Ajaigarh, Bijawar, Nagod, Maihar
regions.note: Smaller states of the Central India Agency (Malwa, Bhopawar, Bundelkhand and Baghelkhand agencies), with the detached Malwa districts of Gwalior and Indore. The many small states and interlocking enclaves cannot be drawn singly from the 1909 map. All acceded in 1947–48. Drawn area c. 28,100 km².

regions.name: Central India Agency (other states): Datia, Samthar
regions.note: Smaller states of the Central India Agency (Malwa, Bhopawar, Bundelkhand and Baghelkhand agencies), with the detached Malwa districts of Gwalior and Indore. The many small states and interlocking enclaves cannot be drawn singly from the 1909 map. All acceded in 1947–48. Drawn area c. 6,800 km².

regions.name: Central India Agency (other states): Charkhari
regions.note: Smaller states of the Central India Agency (Malwa, Bhopawar, Bundelkhand and Baghelkhand agencies), with the detached Malwa districts of Gwalior and Indore. The many small states and interlocking enclaves cannot be drawn singly from the 1909 map. All acceded in 1947–48. Drawn area c. 500 km².

regions.name: Central India Agency (other states): small Bundelkhand states near Baoni
regions.note: Smaller states of the Central India Agency (Malwa, Bhopawar, Bundelkhand and Baghelkhand agencies), with the detached Malwa districts of Gwalior and Indore. The many small states and interlocking enclaves cannot be drawn singly from the 1909 map. All acceded in 1947–48. Drawn area c. 400 km².

regions.name: Kathiawar states
regions.note: The many states of the Kathiawar peninsula (among them Nawanagar, Bhavnagar, Porbandar, Gondal, Morvi and Dhrangadhra). Grouped because they cannot be drawn singly. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 43,400 km².

regions.name: Gujarat states: Palanpur, Radhanpur, Idar, Rajpipla, Lunavada, Chhota Udaipur
regions.note: States of the Palanpur, Mahi Kantha and Rewa Kantha agencies and other Gujarat states under the Bombay government. Grouped because they cannot be drawn singly. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 36,700 km².

regions.name: Gujarat states: tract near Cambay
regions.note: States of the Palanpur, Mahi Kantha and Rewa Kantha agencies and other Gujarat states under the Bombay government. Grouped because they cannot be drawn singly. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 1,400 km².

regions.name: Gujarat states: Dharampur and Bansda
regions.note: States of the Palanpur, Mahi Kantha and Rewa Kantha agencies and other Gujarat states under the Bombay government. Grouped because they cannot be drawn singly. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 1,100 km².

regions.name: Deccan states: Sangli, Miraj, Jamkhandi, Mudhol, Ramdurg, Jath
regions.note: The Southern Maratha Country states and Satara jagirs (Sangli, Miraj, Jamkhandi, Mudhol, Bhor, Aundh, Phaltan, Akalkot and others) and Savantvadi, under the Bombay government. Grouped. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 9,600 km².

regions.name: Deccan states: Bhor
regions.note: The Southern Maratha Country states and Satara jagirs (Sangli, Miraj, Jamkhandi, Mudhol, Bhor, Aundh, Phaltan, Akalkot and others) and Savantvadi, under the Bombay government. Grouped. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 2,300 km².

regions.name: Deccan states: Savantvadi
regions.note: The Southern Maratha Country states and Satara jagirs (Sangli, Miraj, Jamkhandi, Mudhol, Bhor, Aundh, Phaltan, Akalkot and others) and Savantvadi, under the Bombay government. Grouped. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 1,700 km².

regions.name: Deccan states: small tract south of Kolhapur
regions.note: The Southern Maratha Country states and Satara jagirs (Sangli, Miraj, Jamkhandi, Mudhol, Bhor, Aundh, Phaltan, Akalkot and others) and Savantvadi, under the Bombay government. Grouped. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 1,600 km².

regions.name: Deccan states: Phaltan
regions.note: The Southern Maratha Country states and Satara jagirs (Sangli, Miraj, Jamkhandi, Mudhol, Bhor, Aundh, Phaltan, Akalkot and others) and Savantvadi, under the Bombay government. Grouped. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 800 km².

regions.name: Deccan states: Akalkot
regions.note: The Southern Maratha Country states and Satara jagirs (Sangli, Miraj, Jamkhandi, Mudhol, Bhor, Aundh, Phaltan, Akalkot and others) and Savantvadi, under the Bombay government. Grouped. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 600 km².

regions.name: Deccan states: small tract near Kurundvad
regions.note: The Southern Maratha Country states and Satara jagirs (Sangli, Miraj, Jamkhandi, Mudhol, Bhor, Aundh, Phaltan, Akalkot and others) and Savantvadi, under the Bombay government. Grouped. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 400 km².

regions.name: Chhattisgarh feudatory states: Raigarh, Sarangarh, Sakti, Korea, Jashpur, Udaipur (Dharamjaigarh)
regions.note: Feudatory states of the Central Provinces (later the Chhattisgarh States Agency). Merged into the Central Provinces on 1 January 1948. Drawn area c. 18,500 km².

regions.name: Chhattisgarh feudatory states: Nandgaon, Khairagarh
regions.note: Feudatory states of the Central Provinces (later the Chhattisgarh States Agency). Merged into the Central Provinces on 1 January 1948. Drawn area c. 4,300 km².

regions.name: Chhattisgarh feudatory states: Kanker
regions.note: Feudatory states of the Central Provinces (later the Chhattisgarh States Agency). Merged into the Central Provinces on 1 January 1948. Drawn area c. 4,300 km².

regions.name: Chhattisgarh feudatory states: Kawardha
regions.note: Feudatory states of the Central Provinces (later the Chhattisgarh States Agency). Merged into the Central Provinces on 1 January 1948. Drawn area c. 3,000 km².

regions.name: Orissa feudatory states: Patna, Kalahandi, Sonpur, Bamra, Gangpur, Keonjhar, Dhenkanal, Bonai, Nayagarh, Baud, Talcher, Nilgiri, Athmallik
regions.note: The Orissa Tributary States; with the Chhattisgarh states they were later grouped in the Eastern States Agency. Merger agreements of December 1947 took effect on 1 January 1948. Drawn area c. 60,000 km².

regions.name: Saraikela and Kharsawan (Chota Nagpur states)
regions.note: Two small Chota Nagpur states under Bengal in 1909; later in the Eastern States Agency. Merged on 1 January 1948. Drawn area c. 1,500 km².

regions.name: Punjab hill states: Mandi, Suket, Bilaspur, Sirmur, Nalagarh
regions.note: Hill states under the Punjab government (Chamba, Mandi, Suket, Bilaspur, Sirmur, Bashahr and the Simla Hill States). Grouped. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 19,400 km².

regions.name: Punjab hill states: Chamba
regions.note: Hill states under the Punjab government (Chamba, Mandi, Suket, Bilaspur, Sirmur, Bashahr and the Simla Hill States). Grouped. Acceded to India in 1947. Drawn area c. 7,000 km².

regions.name: Punjab states: Jind (Dadri)
regions.note: Plains states under the Punjab government (Nabha, Jind, Faridkot, Kapurthala, Malerkotla and others). Grouped. Acceded to India in 1947 (Bahawalpur, the largest, is drawn separately). Drawn area c. 3,000 km².

regions.name: Punjab states: Faridkot
regions.note: Plains states under the Punjab government (Nabha, Jind, Faridkot, Kapurthala, Malerkotla and others). Grouped. Acceded to India in 1947 (Bahawalpur, the largest, is drawn separately). Drawn area c. 2,200 km².

regions.name: Punjab states: Jind
regions.note: Plains states under the Punjab government (Nabha, Jind, Faridkot, Kapurthala, Malerkotla and others). Grouped. Acceded to India in 1947 (Bahawalpur, the largest, is drawn separately). Drawn area c. 2,100 km².

regions.name: Punjab states: Kapurthala
regions.note: Plains states under the Punjab government (Nabha, Jind, Faridkot, Kapurthala, Malerkotla and others). Grouped. Acceded to India in 1947 (Bahawalpur, the largest, is drawn separately). Drawn area c. 1,100 km².
